Second-look procedures involve follow-up surgery after the
original surgery or adjuvant treatment to check for the pres-
ence or absence of disease, especially in cancers that tend to 
recur locally. Th is type of surgery is not used as often today as
it was in the past because of the development and use of less
invasive diagnostic procedures.
Cancer Diagnoses Requiring Surgery Th is sec-
tion reviews the more common diagnoses requiring surgery 
for treatment. Nutritional concerns are of high importance
for those surgical procedures that have impact on nutritional 
intake, digestion, and/or absorption. Chapters 14 and 15 also
address common gastrointestinal surgical procedures and their
resulting nutritional concerns.
Signiﬁ cant and long-term nutritional side eﬀ ects due to cancer
surgery are seen most often for head and neck surgery and gas-
tric surgery (partial and total gastrectomy). Surgical procedures 
may potentially alter an individual’s physical appearance (mas-
tectomy), alter organ function (colostomy), or both (radical 
neck dissection), which can contribute to depression and result 
in reduced food intake and weight loss.
